name: Mind as uniform across living things
plain_explanation: Anaxagoras thought mind is the same in quality in every living thing, including animals; humans only seem smarter because they have hands, not because their minds are inherently superior.
precise_definition: The claim that nous is uniform and equally present ('just as good') in animals as in man, with apparent differences of intelligence between species attributed entirely to bodily differences, especially the possession of hands.
why_it_mattered: An unusually egalitarian and materialist twist on the mind-doctrine, since it denies any qualitative superiority of human reason over animal reason.
examples: Man's apparent superiority attributed to having hands, not superior mind
